name: A set-up step labels what it gives to copy: a shell command, or a line of a unit file
summary: What a set-up step gives an operator to copy says what it is. GET /v1/projects/{id}/setup sends, for each host step, `commands`: entries with a label, the text, a note and a kind: shell (pasted into a shell on the server as it stands), shell-fill (a shell command with words to replace, named in `replace`) or unit-line (a line of a systemd unit file, not a command). Shell commands begin as the host says (interpreter, admin.py of the installed kit, --root, through install/current), from admin.host_command; the endpoint's setup-status answer carries `admin` and, in its backup block, `run_now`, `check` and `unit_directory` beside the ExecStart `line`. The backup step gives the command that runs a backup now, the line for a schedule with where it goes, and the check; its detail says which of the two is missing, a run or a schedule. admin.py add-project prints the same three, labelled. The page shows each entry under its label with its own copy button. A test pastes every shell entry into sh -c.
